Dear Dr. Reynolds,

Thank you for agreeing to evaluate Julian, a 5-year-old boy whose systemic issues began during infancy at approximately five months of age. He lives at home with his parents, and his family history is non-contributory.

Julian presents with recurrent spikes in body temperature, frequently reaching 39 degrees Celsius without an identifiable infectious source. On physical examination, he is well-nourished, and his cardiac and respiratory exams are normal. However, he exhibits prominent bilateral cervical and inguinal nodal enlargement. Abdominal examination demonstrates marked dual enlargement, with the liver edge palpable four centimeters below the right costal margin and the spleen extending three centimeters beneath the left costal margin.

Additionally, Julian has suffered from widespread, intensely pruritic, scaly erythematous patches over his trunk and flexural creases resembling severe eczema. Recent laboratory workup demonstrates persistent transaminitis indicative of active liver inflammation, alongside broad serological markers demonstrating marked self-reactive antibody production and immune-mediated targeting. His basic renal function and urinalysis have consistently been unremarkable, and his developmental milestones remain on track.

Given the chronic and multi-system nature of his findings, I would value your comprehensive assessment regarding further workup and therapeutic strategies.

Sincerely,
Dr. Arthur Vance
